title: Time-weighted averages and integrals
description: Use time-weighted averages and integrals for time-series data that is not evenly sampled

import * as C from "@constants";
import { NumberedList, NumberedItem } from "@components/NumberedList";
import TestPlan from "@components/TestPlan.astro";

When samples land at uneven intervals, a simple mean can overweight short spikes or underweight long plateaus. **Time-weighted averages** and integrals assign each reading weight proportional to how long it was in effect, so irregular sampling still reflects duration correctly. Evenly spaced series (for example every 30 seconds) rarely need this; irregular bursts or adaptive sampling do.

For example, if you have a lot of ice cream in freezers, you need to make sure
the ice cream stays within a 0-10℉ (-18 to -12℃) temperature range. The
temperature in the freezer can vary if folks are opening and closing the door,
but the ice cream only has a problem if the temperature is out of range
for a long time. You can set your sensors in the freezer to sample every five
minutes while the temperature is in range, and every 30 seconds while the
temperature is out of range. If the results are generally stable, but with some
quick moving transients, an average of all the data points weights the transient
values too highly. A time weighted average weights each value by the duration
over which it occurred based on the points around it, producing much more
accurate results.

Time weighted integrals are useful when you need a time-weighted sum of
irregularly sampled data. For example, if you bill your users based on
irregularly sampled CPU usage, you need to find the total area under the graph
of their CPU usage. You can use a time-weighted integral to find the total
CPU-hours used by a user over a given time period.

For more information about how time-weighted averages work, read the
[time-weighted averages blog](https://www.tigerdata.com/blog/what-time-weighted-averages-are-and-why-you-should-care).

## Run a time-weighted average query

Time weighted average in {C.TIMESCALE_DB} is implemented as an aggregate that
weights each value using last observation carried forward (LOCF), or linear
interpolation. The aggregate is not parallelizable, but it is supported with
[{C.CAGG}s](/build/continuous-aggregates/create-a-continuous-aggregate).

In this procedure, we use an example table called `freezer_temps` that
contains data about internal freezer temperatures:

```sql
CREATE TABLE freezer_temps (freezer_id INTEGER NOT NULL, ts TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL, temperature DOUBLE PRECISION) WITH (tsdb.hypertable, tsdb.partition_column = 'ts');
```

<NumberedList>
<NumberedItem title="Find the average and the time-weighted average">
```sql
SELECT freezer_id,
  avg(temperature),
 average(time_weight('Linear', ts, temperature)) as time_weighted_average
FROM freezer_temps
GROUP BY freezer_id;
```
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title="Use a time-weighted average in a window function">
To determine if the freezer has been out of temperature range for more
than 15 minutes at a time:

```sql
SELECT *,
average(
        time_weight('Linear', ts, temperature) OVER (PARTITION BY freezer_id ORDER BY ts RANGE  '15 minutes'::interval PRECEDING )
       ) as rolling_twa
FROM freezer_temps
ORDER BY freezer_id, ts;
```
</NumberedItem>
</NumberedList>

For more information about time-weighted average API calls, see the
[hyperfunction API documentation](/reference/toolkit/time_weight/time_weight).

target: cloud, self-hosted

1. fork the service
2. [cloud] select the service
3. [self-hosted] run command: `echo 'APT::Get::Assume-Yes "true";' > /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/90doctest`
4. [self-hosted] run command: `apt update`
5. [self-hosted] run command: `apt install timescaledb-toolkit-postgresql-18`
6. [self-hosted] run SQL: `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS timescaledb;`
7. [self-hosted] run SQL: `CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS timescaledb_toolkit;`
8. run SQL: `CREATE TABLE freezer_temps (freezer_id INTEGER NOT NULL, ts TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL, temperature DOUBLE PRECISION) WITH (tsdb.hypertable, tsdb.partition_column = 'ts');`
9. run SQL: `INSERT INTO freezer_temps SELECT 1, '2026-01-01 00:00+00'::timestamptz + (m || ' minutes')::interval, 5 FROM generate_series(0, 50, 5) AS m;`
10. run SQL: `INSERT INTO freezer_temps SELECT 1, '2026-01-01 00:50:30+00'::timestamptz + (s || ' seconds')::interval, 20 FROM generate_series(0, 90, 30) AS s;`
11. run SQL: `INSERT INTO freezer_temps VALUES (1, '2026-01-01 00:55+00', 5), (1, '2026-01-01 01:00+00', 5);`
12. run SQL: `INSERT INTO freezer_temps SELECT 2, '2026-01-01 00:00+00'::timestamptz + (m || ' minutes')::interval, 5 FROM generate_series(0, 60, 5) AS m;`
13. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM pg_proc WHERE proname = 'time_weight' AND prokind = 'a' AND proparallel = 'u'`
14. run SQL: `SELECT freezer_id, avg(temperature), average(time_weight('Linear', ts, temperature)) as time_weighted_average FROM freezer_temps GROUP BY freezer_id;`
15. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM (SELECT freezer_id, avg(temperature) AS mean, average(time_weight('Linear', ts, temperature)) AS twa FROM freezer_temps GROUP BY freezer_id) t WHERE freezer_id = 1 AND mean > 8 AND twa BETWEEN 5.5 AND 6.5`
16. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM (SELECT freezer_id, avg(temperature) AS mean, average(time_weight('Linear', ts, temperature)) AS twa FROM freezer_temps GROUP BY freezer_id) t WHERE freezer_id = 2 AND mean = 5 AND abs(twa - 5) < 1e-9`
17. run SQL: `SELECT *, average(time_weight('Linear', ts, temperature) OVER (PARTITION BY freezer_id ORDER BY ts RANGE '15 minutes'::interval PRECEDING)) as rolling_twa FROM freezer_temps ORDER BY freezer_id, ts;`
18. expect rows: `SELECT 1 FROM (SELECT freezer_id, ts, average(time_weight('Linear', ts, temperature) OVER (PARTITION BY freezer_id ORDER BY ts RANGE '15 minutes'::interval PRECEDING)) AS rolling_twa FROM freezer_temps) t HAVING count(*) = 30 AND count(rolling_twa) = 28 AND max(rolling_twa) FILTER (WHERE freezer_id = 1) BETWEEN 8 AND 9 AND max(rolling_twa) FILTER (WHERE freezer_id = 2) < 5.000001`
</TestPlan>
